newsitem.title: UK: BAA, Railtrack rise on windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: BAA, Railtrack rise on windfall tax.

text.p: Shares in BAA Plc and Railtrack Plc rose in pre-market trading on Thursday after the Labour government's windfall tax on them was viewed as lower than expected, traders said.
BAA was quoted up 8p at 580-1/2p and Railtrack gained 7p to 639p.
"That is the essence of it that it was lighter than expected and that is why (BAA) is being marked up," one trader said.
UK airports operator BAA said on Wednesday that an initial assessment of its windfall tax exposure put the levy at between 70 million and 100 million stg.
BAA said it would have to borrow to pay for the tax but it does not intend to mount a legal challenge.
Railtrack, the rail infrastructure group, raised its figure for the potential hit from an original estimate of 80 million to 135 million stg, to as high as 160 million stg.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown detailed the windfall tax on privatised utilities on Wednesday in his first budget since Labour took power in May.
The government said it would raise 5.2 billion pounds through a tax on privatised utilities, much as expected.
